edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.population: adults with low baseline vitamin D
edges.mechanism: Vitamin D signaling affects calcium handling, immune tone, renin-angiotensin activity, and skeletal muscle, but supplementation only changes those pathways meaningfully when baseline status is low. That helps explain why effects on Cardiovascular disease are usually clearest in deficiency and muted in already replete adults.
edges.summary: In adults with low baseline vitamin D, pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest that vitamin d in deficient adults tracks with lower risk of cardiovascular disease. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
